India EBITDA margin was 18.6% in Q1 CY25 including a one-off mega subsidy at Zaheerabad; excluding it, margin was 18%, up from 17.7% in Q1 CY24 and 17.1% in Q4 CY24.
Europe EBITDA margin was 13.9% in Q1 CY25, down from 15.5% in Q1 CY24 and 14.9% in Q4 CY24 due to lower sales and restructuring costs.
Management expects Europe pain to continue for at least a couple more quarters; India volume growth seen at 4-7% for the year, aiming to beat market.
New order allocation in Q1 CY25 was Rs 3.5 billion, higher than internal budget and target; annual order book generation typically Rs 800-1,000 crores.
India margins expected to improve steadily through operating efficiencies, not dramatically; Europe margins to be held around 14% despite sales declines via restructuring.
Capacity utilization affected by delayed EV and ICE program ramps; customers expect ICE projects to double output in 2-3 months then reach full volume.
Consolidated maintenance capex for H1 CY2025 was ₹610 million
India Q2 CY25 EBITDA margin 17.5%, marginally lower YoY and sequentially due to product mix; Q1 CY25 reported 18.6% included one-time government grant, underlying ~18%
Europe Q2 CY25 EBITDA margin 12.5% includes one-time Metalcastello restructuring cost; without it margin would be closer to 15%
Expect H2 CY25 better than H1 in India due to good monsoon and festive season; Europe H2 normally worse than H1 by ~15% due to seasonality
Europe market expected to remain at current weak level for next 1-2 quarters; customers indicate recovery by beginning next year but not certain
New order book INR3.5bn in Q1 CY25, ~INR6bn in H1 CY25; trend continuing, order book healthy
H1 CY25 growth capex INR0.7bn focused on India projects; expect full year capex close to 5% of revenue guidance as H2 ramps up with new projects
Europe recurrent EBITDA margin expected around 14-15% even in current market conditions; India margins expected to improve slightly with sales recovery
India EBITDA margin 17.3% in Q3 CY25, lower YoY and QoQ due to Maharashtra energy tariff hike; impact 0-0.5% to be offset in coming quarters.
India market 3-year CAGR could improve 2.5-3% points due to GST optimization; PV CAGR may rise from 2-3% to 5-6%, 2W similarly.
Europe EBITDA margin 14.1% in Q3 CY25, lower YoY but higher QoQ; adjusted for Q2 restructuring, margins roughly flat sequentially.
Europe light vehicle production forecast flat at 16-17 million units for 2025-2027; IHS sees -1.5% for CY26.
Aluminum business EBITDA improved from ~10% (2019) to ~15% now; targeting further gains via tech transfer, higher value-add, machining, assembly.
Metalcastello stabilized at ~45M EUR/year turnover; exporting to Caterpillar US; expects mid-term recovery in off-highway.
India GST cut structural, not one-time; longer-term impact expected but festive season and inventory corrections cloud near-term read.
CIE philosophy: same target EBITDA margin regardless of EV/ICE, geography, or segment (ferrous vs aluminum).
Mexico stable margins ~Europe; growth slowed as US BEV subsidy cut delays awarded battery EV program 2-3 years.
IHS forecasts Light Vehicle production growth of 7.4% and MHCV growth of 5.3% for CY26
CRISIL expects 2W production to grow 8-10% for CY26
India Q4 CY25 EBITDA margin 16.8% vs 17.1% YoY; adjusted for energy tariff (+0.3%) and gratuity one-off (+0.8%) would be 17.9%
Europe Q4 CY25 EBITDA margin 12.7% vs 14.9% YoY; adjusted for EUR2m restructuring at Legazpi (2.5% of sales) would be above 15%
CY25 new order wins: INR8.7bn/year in India (10% EV, 90% ICE) and INR2.1bn/year in Europe

Expanding capacity across India verticals: composites, stampings, aluminum, iron foundry; transferring some European presses and gear cells to India by April; iron castings export program SOP June CY26
India growth trajectory improving quarterly (7%, 9%, 12% in last 3 quarters); expects trend to continue; margins to improve in India, protect in Europe; CY26 capex higher than CY25
Capital expenditure contracted but not recognized as liabilities Rs 93.25 crore
India market estimates 8-10% growth for CY2026, tapering Q3 onwards
Management expects calendar year 2026 to be a good year with continued growth trend across all verticals, barring major geopolitical impact.
India EBITDA margin was 17.6% in Q1 CY26 vs 18.6% a year ago; drop due to gas/material cost increases, Maharashtra energy tariff hike, and absence of INR87M one-off subsidy.
Europe EBITDA margin recovered to 15.7% in Q1 CY26 from 13.9% a year ago and 12.7% in Q4 CY25 due to restructuring activities in CY25.
New order intake in Q1 CY26 was INR3.5 billion annualized turnover, with approximately 11% for EV sector.
India growth capex will be significantly higher in CY26 and CY27; Q1 CY26 capex was ~INR900M (~6% of sales); full year guidance INR4-5 billion.
Adding capacity across all verticals except magnets: 3 new forging lines, stamping lines, iron casting molding line; capacity aligned with new order ramp-up.
Consolidated maintenance capex H1 CY2026 INR 876 million
Management targets 12-15% growth for India operations going forward, aiming to outperform market but acknowledging some quarters may be slightly below
India EBITDA margin 16.7% in Q2 CY26 vs 17.5% YoY and 17.6% QoQ, depressed by cost inflation from West Asia conflict affecting energy, consumables and raw materials
Europe EBITDA margin improved to 15.9% in Q2 CY26 from 12.5% YoY and 15.7% QoQ due to last year's restructuring activities
Consolidated EBITDA margin 16.7% in H1 CY26 vs 16.3% in H1 CY25, with PAT margin 9.5% vs 9.1%
New order book of INR5 billion per year secured in H1 CY26, well diversified across verticals, in line with internal targets
Iron foundry export project for US customer ramping up, expected to add INR2,000 million per year revenue, revenue recognition from next quarter

H1 CY26 capex INR2.1 billion vs INR3.8 billion full year CY25; H2 CY26 capex expected significantly higher, focused on India growth projects including machine casting, gears, composites, stampings, forgings

Expanding capacity across verticals: iron foundry new line, gears plants in Rajkot and Chakan, stamping robotic line in Kanhe by mid next year, forging presses in Chakan and Bengaluru, evaluating brownfield and greenfield projects

Greenfield expansions planned in two verticals driven by customer location requests, also prioritizing four-wheeler aluminum diversification (currently INR500-750 million), EV composites and gears, and iron casting exports
Expect relative slowing in India market growth over next few quarters as effect of GST cuts diminish
India EBITDA margin 16.3% in Q3 CY26 vs 17.3% in Q3 CY25 and 16.7% in Q2 CY26; drop due to price pressures from West Asia conflict in raw material, energy, consumables
Europe EBITDA margin 16.3% in Q3 CY26 vs 14.1% in Q3 CY25 and 15.9% in Q2 CY26; recovery due to last year's restructuring
Order book healthy in Q3; INR9.7 billion new orders in India YTD 9 months CY26 across all verticals; approx INR3 billion in Europe

CY26 India capex almost double last year; next year similar range; investing across all verticals including forging presses, gear plant expansion, composite presses, stamping line, foundry expansion by 2028

Aluminum diversifying into 4-wheeler HPDC parts requiring new lines; Stampings expanding at multiple locations for 2 main customers; Gears and Composites have EV orders; Iron castings near full foundry capacity planning expansion; Forgings
One press from Bill Forge Mexico being transferred to Hosur, India; press dismantled, expected receipt in Q1 2027
Growth capex ~8% of sales in India (vs usual 5%); CY26 approx double last year; CY27 similar range; all verticals expanding with booked orders
India market demand robust but slowing in next quarters as GST cuts fade; tractor growth slower than other segments
Foundry division fully booked for next year post new American customer project ramp-up
India market demand robust but slowing in next quarters due to fading GST impact; tractor growth slower than other segments
India order book strong at ₹9.7B YTD (9M CY26), Europe at ~₹3B; new projects (e.g., foundry for US customer) starting Q4
India market demand growth to slow in next few quarters due to fading GST cut impact
